label: Parte 4
subtitle: Tema abstracto · 2 min · DONDE MÁS NOTA SE JUEGA

meta.formato: 3 preguntas sobre un tema · UNA respuesta combinada de 2 min

objetivo: Una sola respuesta de 2 min que cubre las 3 preguntas con conectores tipo 'Regarding the first… / Moving on to the second… / Finally…'. Las 3 preguntas son: Q1 experiencia pasada (memoria personal), Q2 cómo lo gestionas / sentimiento, Q3 opinión general / especulación abstracta. Variedad gramatical (presente, pasado simple, pasado continuo, futuro, condicional 2 y perfecto) + idioms C1 + inversión opcional.

patron_oficial.descripcion: Q1 normalmente pide una experiencia pasada ('Tell me about a time when…'). Q2 pide cómo lo gestionas o cómo te hizo sentir. Q3 pide tu opinión sobre el tema en general ('Do you think people…?'). Se contesta TODO en un único bloque de 2 minutos, marcando claramente cada respuesta con conectores.
ejemplo_real: Q1 (experiencia pasada): Tell me about a time when you were stressed out.
Q2 (gestión / sentimiento): How do you usually deal with stress?
Q3 (opinión general): Why do you think people feel more stressed nowadays?

estrategia_2min: Estructura: 1) Apertura impersonal (~15 seg) para 'romper el hielo'. 2) Q1: 'Regarding the first question, …' (~40 seg, experiencia pasada con pasado simple + continuo). 3) Q2: 'Moving on to the second question, …' (~35 seg, cómo lo gestionas, presente + condicional). 4) Q3: 'Finally, regarding the third question, …' (~30 seg, opinión general + futuro + idiom de cierre).

pasos.title: Apertura impersonal · romper el hielo

plantilla_segmentos.texto: has become increasingly relevant in modern society. From my point of view, these kinds of situations are very common nowadays, especially in our fast-paced world.

tema.ayuda: El tema del que toca hablar.

pasos.trick: 'It's widely recognised that…' = pasiva impersonal C1. Suena académico al instante. Memorízala como un padrenuestro.
trucos_examen: TIEMPO VERBAL: presente perfecto + presente simple.
PISTA: la apertura es UNIVERSAL. Solo cambia el sustantivo del hueco. Memorízala.
MARCA C1: pasiva impersonal 'It's widely recognised that' es de las estructuras más rentables del examen.
EVITA: empezar con 'I think that…' o 'In my opinion'. Quema munición C1 de entrada.

pasos.title: Beneficio principal + tendencia

plantilla_segmentos.texto: . One of the main advantages is that it helps us
. What's more, more and more people are

beneficio.ayuda: Beneficio principal. Verbo en infinitivo SIN to.

opciones.texto: stay connected with our loved ones

tendencia.ayuda: Tras 'more and more people are…' va -ing.

pasos.trick: 'More and more + sujeto + are + -ing' = comparativo progresivo + presente continuo de tendencia. Doble jugada B2.
trucos_examen: TIEMPO VERBAL: presente perfecto ('has transformed') + presente simple ('helps') + presente continuo ('are -ing').
MARCA C1: 'broaden our horizons' / 'relate to each other' / 'embracing change' son colocaciones puras.
TRUCO: este paso es el más rentable del examen. Combina 3 tiempos verbales y 2 estructuras avanzadas.
EVITA: 'many people' (plano). USA 'more and more people are -ing' (progresivo).

pasos.title: Contraargumento (matiza)

plantilla_segmentos.texto: also has some drawbacks, such as
. Although it's generally beneficial, we shouldn't overlook the fact that

problema1.ayuda: Tras 'such as' SOLO sustantivos o gerundios. NUNCA infinitivos.

matiz.ayuda: Frase con sujeto + verbo que matiza el problema.

opciones.texto: not everyone has equal access to it
its long-term effects are still unclear
it requires a lot of self-discipline

pasos.trick: 'Overlook' > 'forget'. 'We shouldn't overlook the fact that…' es estructura C1 pura.
pasos.warning: Tras 'such as' SOLO sustantivos o gerundios, NUNCA infinitivos. Error típico de B1.
trucos_examen: TIEMPO VERBAL: presente simple (verdad general).
MARCA C1: 'we shouldn't overlook the fact that' + cláusula = densidad discursiva alta.
GRAMÁTICA: tras 'such as' SIEMPRE sustantivo o -ing. NUNCA infinitivo.
EVITA: 'such as to wait' (ERROR). USA 'such as waiting' o 'such as the wait'.

pasos.title: Experiencia personal · storytelling
pasos.grammar: Pasado simple + pasado continuo · LA CLAVE

alternativas.texto: This reminds me of the time when
I'll never forget the time when
There was this one time when

plantilla_segmentos.texto: This reminds me of the time when I

accion1.ayuda: Acción puntual y concreta en pasado.

opciones.texto: decided to disconnect from social media for a week
took up running as a way to clear my mind
moved to a new city for work reasons
looked after my little nephew for a whole weekend
had a really demanding project at work

accion2.ayuda: Pasado continuo. La combinación con el paso anterior es la marca B2-alto.

opciones.texto: scrolling through Instagram late at night and realised I'd wasted three hours
working overtime and felt completely drained
walking around a small town and felt completely amazed
preparing dinner for the whole family and felt really fulfilled

leccion.ayuda: Qué aprendiste. Frase con sujeto + verbo.

opciones.texto: stepping out of your comfort zone really opens your mind

pasos.trick: Mezclar pasado simple + pasado continuo en una sola frase = demostración de control gramatical B2 alto. Imprescindible para C1.

upgrades_c1.ejemplo: Hardly had I started running when I felt completely energised.
upgrades_c1.uso: Sustituye al pasado simple básico. Inversión potente, una sola por respuesta.

upgrades_c1.ejemplo: Little did I know that this small change would transform my routine.
upgrades_c1.uso: Cierra la narración con efecto sorpresa.

trucos_examen: TIEMPO VERBAL: pasado simple + pasado continuo en frases encadenadas.
MARCA C1: la inversión 'Hardly had I… when' o 'Little did I know that' eleva una nota entera. Una sola por respuesta.
TRUCO: este paso es donde respondes la Q1 (experiencia pasada). Conector recomendado: 'Regarding the first question, this reminds me of…'
EVITA: pasado perfecto continuo ('I had been doing'). Casi siempre mal construido. USA pasado simple + continuo.

pasos.title: Hipótesis y futuro

conector_inicial.texto: If I were in this situation,

alternativas.texto: If I were in this situation,

plantilla_segmentos.texto: If I were in this situation, I would probably
. In the future, I think people will

accion_cond.ayuda: Tras 'I would probably' va infinitivo sin to.

opciones.texto: look for a better work-life balance
become more aware of its impact

causa.ayuda: Por qué pasará lo que dices.

pasos.trick: 'If I WERE' (no 'was') con todos los sujetos. Es la forma B2 correcta del condicional 2.
pasos.warning: 'If I am… I will…' = ERROR. Hipótesis = condicional 2: 'If I were… I would…'.
trucos_examen: TIEMPO VERBAL: condicional 2 ('If I WERE… I WOULD') + futuro will.
MARCA C1: inversión 'Were I in this situation' es 1 punto más que 'If I were'.
TRUCO: este paso responde la Q3 (opinión / futuro). Conector recomendado: 'Finally, regarding the third question, I think people will…'
EVITA: 'If I was'. La forma correcta en condicional 2 SIEMPRE es 'If I WERE' (con todos los sujetos).

pasos.title: Cierre con idiom C1

alternativas.texto: At the end of the day,

plantilla_segmentos.texto: is a double-edged sword: we just need to find the right balance.

tema_final.ayuda: Repite el tema una última vez.

pasos.trick: Tres idioms en el cierre: 'in a nutshell' + 'double-edged sword' + 'find the right balance'. Si solo recuerdas uno, que sea este.
trucos_examen: TIEMPO VERBAL: presente simple.
MARCA C1: 'in a nutshell' + 'double-edged sword' + 'find the right balance' = TRES idioms en una frase.
TEMA: UNIVERSAL — el cierre completo funciona para CUALQUIER tema de Parte 4.
EVITA: silencio o 'and that's all'. El cierre con triple idiom es la marca registrada de un C1.

bloque_a: Tell me about a time when you were stressed out.

bloque_c: Do you think people work better under pressure?

temas.respuesta_modelo_a: Regarding the first question, this reminds me of the time when I had a really demanding project at work last year. I remember once I was working overtime late at night and felt completely drained, and I learnt that setting limits really matters. Hardly had I started organising my time when everything began to fall into place. It was one of those experiences that really stayed with me.
temas.respuesta_modelo_b: Moving on to the second question, I usually try to manage stress by sticking to a routine. I make a point of doing some sport every week and taking regular breaks during the day. If I were in this situation again, I would probably set clearer boundaries between work and personal life. Honestly, it just feels far more manageable that way.
temas.respuesta_modelo_c: Finally, regarding the third question, I think people do tend to work better under pressure, at least up to a point. There's no denying that deadlines push us to focus, but more and more people are looking for a healthier balance these days. In the future, I expect employers will pay more attention to wellbeing, especially due to growing awareness. In a nutshell, stress is a double-edged sword: we just need to find the right balance.
